content.learning_goal: Enable Grade 7 learners to understand and apply the central ideas of Life Processes in Animals.

explanation_sections.title: Activate
explanation_sections.explanation: Connect the chapter to prior knowledge, observation or experience.

explanation_sections.title: Build
explanation_sections.explanation: Teach from the source-grounded points and examples.
source_evidence: Life Processes 9 in Animals If your food is fully digested before you eat again, you won’t need medicine for pain.

(Thirukkural 942) In the Grade 6 Science textbook Curiosity, chapter ‘Living Creatures: Exploring their Characteristics’, we learnt about processes essential for survival of living beings like nutrition, respiration, excretion, and reproduction.
In this chapter, we will learn about life processes such as nutrition and respiration in detail.
Bees and sunbirds suck the nectar of ﬂowers, while infants of humans and many other animals feed on their mother’s milk.
Some aquatic animals ﬁlter tiny food particles ﬂoating nearby and feed upon them.

explanation_sections.title: Reason
explanation_sections.explanation: Ask learners to explain relationships, evidence, patterns or steps.

explanation_sections.title: Transfer
explanation_sections.explanation: Move from the textbook context to a closely related new situation.

misconceptions: Confusing an example with the underlying concept.
checks_for_understanding: What changes if an important condition changes?
content.closure: Learner states the central idea, supporting evidence and one application.
